sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner has Suite 105 on the ground floor of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville, Georgia 31639. For a bill or a payment, call (229) 686-7461. Visitors are welcome on weekdays from eight until five. Real property, personal property, mobile home, motor vehicle and timber tax all run through this one office.

Value is a different office's job. Berrien's Board of Tax Assessors sets it and takes homestead applications, and the commissioner's staff will direct you there if you are unsure.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, receipts, payment help, liens
  • Tax Assessor: values, returns, homestead and other exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies from the courthouse deed room

Berrien is a rural south central Georgia county of 458 square miles, and one school system, the Berrien County School District, covers every address. Population has swung from 19,286 in 2010 to 18,160 and then to an estimated 18,932 for 2025. Nearly three quarters of residents in 2020 lived outside urban areas, so most owners hold rural parcels rather than town lots.

The county has 8,328 housing units in 2025 and a 71.0 percent owner rate. Median household income is $52,876, the middle owner-occupied value is $131,600 and middle gross rent is $782 a month. Only 115 building permits were issued in 2025, so most listings are older farmhouses and country lots, and buyers price them that way.

Every year, houses, land and business equipment are due November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1 instead, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

Each month of delay adds 1% interest. If the bill is still open three months past the deadline, a flat 10% penalty is added. At 30 days overdue, the office can record a FiFa lien with the Clerk of Superior Court, and in the end the commissioner may levy on the parcel.

Owners can search a parcel and pay online through the GovtWindow platform, and the help desk number is (877) 575-7233. A mobile or modular home is personal property in Georgia, which means a yearly return and a location permit, and the permit comes only after that year's tax is paid in full. The commissioner also bills timber tax, a point that matters to anyone selling acreage.

Berrien County payment calendar and late charges
Account typeDueIf late
Real estate and business personal propertyNovember 151% a month, then 10% after 90 days
Mobile and manufactured homesApril 1Location permit needs tax paid in full
Motor vehiclesOwner's birthdayCollected by the same office

Georgia taxes 40% of market value, and Berrien's county commissioners and school board each pick a millage yearly. The sequence is short: start from assessed value, subtract exemptions to reach net taxable value, then multiply by the mills. Each mill raises a dollar on every $1,000 of that net figure.

Rather than guess, ask the commissioner for the millage on your parcel. Statements are mailed to the owner, so a lender that escrows needs a copy. Check that your servicer has the Berrien bill, and keep your own copy for the closing file.

  • Returns: owners can name their own value any time in the first three months of the year
  • Notice: the assessors send one when their value differs from the return
  • Bill: the commissioner applies the mills to net taxable value

Owning the house and living in it on New Year's Day are both required. Send the application to the tax assessor's office so that it arrives before April 1. You can file any time of year, but a late one takes effect the following tax year.

Approval carries over year to year at the same address. A move to another Berrien house means filing anew. Homeowners at 62 may apply for an added exemption, and business personal property can qualify for freeport relief. The dollar figures change with legislation, so the assessors are the source for current amounts.

You have 45 days, counted from the notice date. The appeal is heard by the county Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and if you are still unhappy you notify the Board of Tax Assessors in writing that you are going on to superior court.

A fair market value appeal sent by mail needs a postmark no later than day 45. Tax collected in error or illegally can be recovered when a written claim is made inside three years of payment.

Most Berrien owners hold country land, and that adds a few checks. Timber is taxed and billed by the commissioner, so a seller with standing trees should ask whether any timber tax is open. A mobile home on the land is a separate account with its own April 1 deadline and its own permit.

List each account when you talk to the buyer's side. A clean payoff on the house alone does not tell the title company that the mobile home or timber account is also paid, and a missed one can delay a closing. If the deed came to you through an estate, ask the commissioner whether the bills for earlier years went to a prior owner, and settle them all in one visit so the record is complete before you sign.

Before you accept an offer, ask the commissioner for the balance in writing and confirm who is billed. The statement goes to the January 1 owner, so yours may still show up after a fall closing. Your closing agent can show how that year's tax is divided.

A FiFa on file is public and must be satisfied before the buyer gets a clean title. Farmhouses with old taxes, inherited deeds or deferred repairs can still sell as is, since the payoff is taken from the sale money. A cash buyer will ask for the same payoff number you hold. If the house is a rural parcel, also ask whether any timber tax or a mobile home account is attached to the same owner, since the commissioner bills those too, and settle each one before the deed is signed.

Selling for cash skips the lender appraisal and the repair list, which suits a farmhouse with deferred upkeep. It does not skip the tax payoff. The balance is still paid from your proceeds at the table, so getting the number early keeps the closing date from slipping.

A short list to bring to Suite 105: your deed or parcel number, the latest statement, any lien notice, and the name of your closing agent. Ask for the figures in writing and note the date they are good through, because interest is added each month.

faqs.q: When does Berrien County want its property tax?
faqs.a: November 15 each year covers real estate and business personal property. Mobile homes fall due April 1.

faqs.q: What does overdue Berrien County tax cost?
faqs.a: Interest is 1% a month from the due date, and a 10% penalty follows if 90 days pass without payment.

faqs.q: Where is the Berrien County tax office?
faqs.a: At 201 N. Davis Street, Suite 105, Nashville, inside the Administration Building. The phone is (229) 686-7461 and weekday hours are 8 to 5.

faqs.q: How fast must a Berrien County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Inside 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does the Berrien tax bill go to my lender?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner mails statements to homeowners only. If your lender escrows, forward the bill or confirm the servicer is paying it.
